subject: Computer Networking
title: Email Deliverability
description: A quick win: understand Email Deliverability.

hook.text: You sent a newsletter to 10,000 subscribers. Only 7,000 received it. The rest vanished. Deliverability failed.

buildup.text: Deliverability is the art of reaching the inbox. SPF, DKIM, and DMARC are the minimum requirements.

discovery.text: List hygiene matters: remove bounces and inactive subscribers. High bounce rates destroy your reputation.

twist.text: Even legit emails land in spam. Trigger words, image-heavy layouts, and too many links lower your score.

climax.text: Warm up new IPs slowly: 100 emails on day one, doubling gradually. Sudden spikes trigger spam flags.

punchline.text: Deliverability is earned, not guaranteed. Every detail matters.

quiz.question: Why should you warm up a new sending IP address?
options: Sudden volume spikes trigger spam flags at receiving servers
New IPs are slower and need time to reach full speed
Email protocols require a handshake period for new IPs

details.summary: Email deliverability is the practice of ensuring legitimate emails reach the inbox rather than the spam folder. It depends on sender reputation, authentication configuration, content quality, list hygiene, and sending patterns. Poor deliverability means your emails are sent but never seen.
details.whyItMatters: Deliverability determines whether your emails are actually read. Organizations can lose millions in revenue when important communications land in spam instead of the inbox.
takeaways: Sender reputation is the primary factor in deliverability
SPF, DKIM, and DMARC authentication are required baselines
List hygiene and engagement rates directly affect inbox placement

faq.question: What hurts email deliverability the most?
faq.answer: Sending to invalid addresses that bounce, getting marked as spam by recipients, missing authentication records, sending from shared IPs with bad reputation, and sudden volume spikes. Each of these signals to receiving servers that the sender may not be legitimate.

faq.question: How can organizations improve their deliverability?
faq.answer: Configure SPF, DKIM, and DMARC correctly. Remove bouncing addresses immediately. Only send to people who opted in. Warm up new sending IPs gradually. Monitor feedback loops from ISPs. Consistent sending patterns and high engagement rates build positive reputation.
